Subject: Procurement route question — marketplace vs. direct (co-sell?)

Hi Hannah,

We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot across two lines of business and procurement has asked a few concrete questions I was hoping you could help with:

1) If we buy through AWS Marketplace, how does invoicing/timing work vs a direct Redwood contract? We have fiscal cutoffs and need to confirm whether a marketplace purchase hits our AWS invoice immediately or if there's a delay.

2) Is co-sell with AWS compatible with a marketplace listing, or do we need a direct SOW / MSA with Redwood to enable co-sell credits and joint-sell motions?

3) Any implications for our legal team re: MSA redlines — does buying through marketplace avoid negotiating an MSA with Redwood?

Thanks — if easier we can jump on a quick call next week.

Best,
Liz

Hi Liz — thanks for the clear questions. High-level answers below; I'll follow up with a short playbook and a redlines note for your legal team. Looping in Marissa (partner/pricing) and Karthik (cloud channel) for specifics.

Quick answers:
- Marketplace purchases generally show up on your AWS invoice for the billing period when AWS charges you; that timing depends on your AWS billing cycle — typically monthly. There can be a delay between our provisioning and AWS charging if you use private offers or reserved commitments.
- Co-sell: AWS co-sell and marketplace are compatible, but to collect AWS co-sell incentives we generally need the listing to be co-sell eligible and for the deal to be registered in the AWS partner portal. Some enterprise customers prefer a direct MSA for additional contractual terms even when transacting via marketplace.
- Legal/MSA: Marketplace purchases use AWS terms for the purchase flow; they don't automatically replace the need for an MSA if your legal team wants Redwood-specific terms (data protection, audit rights). Many customers do marketplace for procurement speed and then execute a separate MSA for long-term terms.

I'll attach a concise one-pager and a draft MSA redlines summary. Can you share your AWS billing contact and the fiscal cutoff date?

— Hannah

Liz, Hannah — adding color from the marketplace & co-sell side.

A few practical notes we share with procurement teams:
- If speed-to-production is the priority: Marketplace (private offer if needed) is quickest. You can get a PO confirmed and environment provisioned without an MSA in many cases.
- If you need customized billing terms (net-45, tax handling) or off-cycle invoicing, direct contracting is more flexible; marketplace billing is constrained to AWS billing processes.
- Co-sell eligibility checklist: product listing must be marked as co-sell enabled, deal registration submitted, and AWS partner rep engaged. I can open the registration once you confirm the intended ARR band.
- For the MSA: we can provide a redlines summary so your legal team can see the delta vs AWS marketplace terms. In practice many regulated customers sign an MSA and then use marketplace for convenience; the MSA governs data residency, audit, and indemnities.

I've attached a short MSA redline starter and our co-sell checklist (internal). Happy to host a 30-min session with procurement + your AWS rep.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Manager, Channels & Partnerships — Redwood Inference

On Sat, Nov 21, 2026 at 9:41 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Liz, Hannah — adding color from the marketplace & co-sell side.

Quick add from channel operations:
- Marketplace invoice timing — for AWS-managed billing it posts on the customer's monthly AWS invoice. If you have specific fiscal cutoff needs we can coordinate a private offer with an effective date that aligns to your cycle, but the payment still flows through AWS unless you opt for a direct invoice arrangement.
- Co-sell incentives: AWS will only develop co-sell bookings if the deal is registered and the customer purchase path is visible to the AWS rep. A direct contract + SOW with a co-sell registration is the cleanest path for joint-planning, but it is not strictly required.
- Operational impact: if you expect significant usage spikes during pilot, marketplace private offers can be configured with quotas/burst rules; direct dedicated billing gives you more granular invoicing line items for internal chargeback.

Happy to jump on a call with procurement + their AWS rep to walk through a sample private offer vs direct invoice schedule.
